title: Control weeds manually in plant propagation and landscaping

lessons.title: Knowing weeds
lessons.html:
Knowing weeds

A weed is a plant growing where we do not want it. Weeds take water, food and light from our plants. They make gardens look untidy. Some weeds also hide pests and diseases. In a nursery, weeds in pots make the plants grow slowly and nobody wants to buy them.

Common weeds

WeedHow to know it
Nutgrass (uintjie)Grass-like, with small nuts on the roots under the ground
Black jackSmall yellow flowers, black seeds that stick to clothes
KhakibosTall, strong smell when you crush the leaves
Kweek grass in bedsSpreads with runners above and under the ground
Oxalis (sorrel)Clover-like leaves, small bulbs under the ground
ChickweedLow, soft, small white flowers

Annual and perennial weeds

  • Annual weeds grow from seed and die after one season. Pull them out before they flower and make seed.
  • Perennial weeds live for years. They grow back from roots, runners, bulbs or nuts. You must take out all the roots, or they will grow again.

Weed or plant?

Some young weeds look like young garden plants. If you are not sure, ask your team leader before you pull it out. It is easy to pull out a valuable seedling by mistake.

Invasive plants

Some plants are declared invasive in South Africa, for example lantana and some wattles. They spread and harm the veld and rivers. Tell your team leader if you see them.

Look for weeds every day when you water or walk through the nursery. Weeds are easy to pull when they are small. If you leave them for two weeks, the roots go deep and the job takes much longer.

lessons.title: Removing weeds by hand and with tools
lessons.html:
Removing weeds by hand and with tools

Manual weed control means taking out weeds by hand or with hand tools, without chemicals.

Tools

  • Hands, with gloves, for weeds in pots and between small plants.
  • Hand fork or weeder, to lift roots out of the soil.
  • Hoe, to cut weeds just under the soil in open beds.
  • Garden fork, to dig out perennial weeds with deep roots.
  • Wheelbarrow or bucket, to collect weeds.

How to weed

  1. Weed when the soil is a little damp. Roots come out more easily.
  2. Hold the weed low down, near the soil.
  3. Pull slowly and steadily so the root comes out whole.
  4. Use the hand fork to loosen deep roots first.
  5. Do not damage the roots of the good plants nearby.
  6. Put the weeds in the bucket straight away. Do not leave them on the bed.
  7. Firm the soil back around the good plants.

Using a hoe

Pull the hoe towards you, just under the soil surface. This cuts young weeds. Do not hoe deep near plants. Keep the hoe blade sharp.

Getting rid of weeds

  • Small annual weeds without seeds can go on the compost heap.
  • Weeds with seeds, bulbs, nuts or runners must go in the rubbish, not on the compost. They will grow again.

Prevent weeds

Weed often, before weeds flower. Cover bare soil with mulch. Keep pathways clean.

Safety

Wear gloves; some weeds have thorns or sap that burns. Bend your knees or kneel on a mat. Take short breaks. Look out for snakes, bees and broken glass in long weeds. Wash your hands after work.

Key points

  • A weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted.
  • Pull annual weeds before they make seed.
  • Take out all roots, bulbs and runners of perennial weeds.
  • Ask if you are not sure whether a plant is a weed.
  • Weeds with seeds or bulbs go in the rubbish, not the compost.
